scope.note: Mixin holds assets deposited from Bitcoin, Ethereum and other chains in deposit addresses and hot wallets that back balances on its own ledger (its 'domains' are the gateways for assets from other chains). The drained addresses were deposit addresses and hot wallets whose keys were recoverable from a breached cloud-provider database. Value therefore left the custody of Mixin's cross-chain deposit/withdrawal reserves, so it is coded as a custodial peg. Caveat: the custody is centralized key storage much like an exchange hot wallet; DefiLlama does not flag it as a bridge, while the SoK (Table 8) lists it.

outflow.count_note: Eight successful operator withdrawals (withdrawNative for 10,145 ETH, then seven withdrawToken calls; last 346,994 TUSD), all to one recipient. Each release was preceded about 24 s earlier by an identical call from a second operator address (Etherscan labels HTX 52 and HTX 54), consistent with a two-operator confirmation step; read from explorer data only. A ninth call (AAVE) reverted at 10:22:47; four withdrawToken calls from an unrelated address between 10:49 and 10:53 also reverted. The same operator addresses made further withdrawToken calls on 2023-11-23 (not examined; one sent a 1e18-unit amount to an unlabeled address).
